summary: Erika Hayasaki recounts how a former student, identified as S., harassed sociologist Janani Umamaheswar, her husband Alex Sinha, and Vassar professor Catherine Tan. The harassment began with fake Rate My Professors reviews and a false police report, and escalated into tens of thousands of racist, violent tweets and bogus Title IX complaints sent to their employers. The piece shows how police, Twitter and universities struggle to respond to cross-state online stalking of faculty, especially faculty of color, and cites research and expert calls for better institutional protection.
one_line: A former student's years-long online stalking of Asian American professors exposes how universities, police and platforms fail to protect faculty from harassment.
key_facts: Janani Umamaheswar, then an assistant professor of sociology at Southern Connecticut State University, noticed strange, defamatory Rate My Professors reviews in winter 2019 and into early 2020.

Umamaheswar's web hosting report showed one local IP address visiting her professional website repeatedly at all hours, sometimes over two dozen hits an hour; the same IP also visited her husband Alex Sinha's website.
In December 2019 a student, called S., filed a police report accusing Umamaheswar and two other sociology professors of hacking her laptop and using students to follow her.

Southern Connecticut State administrators from four offices, plus police, dismissed S.'s claims as "factually incorrect, disparaging" and "legally actionable," banned her from campus, sent a cease and desist letter, and police arrested her for harassment.

Umamaheswar moved to George Mason University and Sinha taught at Hofstra University; in March 2022 Catherine Tan of Vassar College alerted them to a Twitter account in S.'s name that had been posting since October 2021.

The account posted at least 40,000 tweets according to Sinha, including racist slurs and violent threats such as "I would like for these professors to die"; Twitter suspended accounts but S. kept returning under new handles like @janedoepow.
In November 2022, S. sent Title IX complaints to Vassar and George Mason falsely accusing Tan and Umamaheswar of sexual harassment.
On November 9th, 2022, Tan publicly tweeted "I have a stalker"; the tweet was shared 4,350 times and received more than 15,000 likes.

Sinha, a lawyer, filed an FBI complaint and police reports, but local police would not arrest across state lines and Poughkeepsie police declined to contact Hamden Police; S. lives in Hamden, Connecticut.
A 2009 study in the Journal of the Scholarship of Teaching and Learning found 52 faculty members reported 87 concerning incidents of student stalking.
One study across eight southwestern universities found 17 percent of students reported being stalked since enrolling in college.
Victoria O'Meara of Royal Roads University says universities rely on punitive models, neglect targets' well-being, and should provide digital protections, training and services like DeleteMe.
Author Erika Hayasaki describes her own 2015 experience with a threatening student and being made to feel like an alarmist by some campus officials.
